entry.title: SBND first results
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. SBND reported its first neutrino-argon cross-section measurement, for muon-neutrino charged-current interactions with a single proton and no pions in the final state. Using a subset of Run 1 data corresponding to 8.8×10^19 protons on target, the analysis selects 12,804 signal candidates with a purity of 91%. The measured cross sections, given as functions of transverse kinematic imbalance variables, discriminate strongly among event-generator predictions. Fermilab presents the result as improving interaction modelling for DUNE.

entry.title: DUNE construction
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Fermilab reports that construction of the Long-Baseline Neutrino Facility is entering its next phase, with critical components arriving. Separately, UK groups have completed half of the 137 Anode Plane Assemblies for DUNE. These are the sensors that will record the electrical signals from neutrino interactions in liquid argon.

entry.title: CONUS+ reactor CEvNS
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. CONUS+ reports a measurement of coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering from reactor antineutrinos on germanium. With an exposure of 1296 kg·days reactor-on, a blind likelihood analysis yields 1555 ± 152 events at 10.2σ, consistent within 0.6 standard deviations with the Standard Model expectation of 1701 ± 198. The result gives sin²θ_W = 0.225 ± 0.022 at a momentum transfer of about 10 MeV. A companion paper describes the run 2 detector performance and background model.

entry.title: Super-Kamiokande DSNB
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. Super-Kamiokande reports an indication of electron antineutrinos from the diffuse supernova neutrino background, using a 5003.0-day dataset and a spectral fit. For a representative model, the best-fit flux is 3.6 (+1.6, −1.5) cm⁻² s⁻¹ above 13.3 MeV, a 2.6σ tension with the null hypothesis. The analysis improves atmospheric-neutrino background rejection and the evaluation of systematic uncertainties. Models with different spectral shapes gave similar significances.

entry.title: KM3NeT
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The KM3NeT Collaboration held its Autumn 2026 meeting in Siracusa, with a five-day programme that included status updates on detector operations. KM3NeT was also recognised as a Landmark in the ESFRI Roadmap 2026. A new review of the ultra-high-energy event KM3-230213A, with an inferred parent-neutrino energy of O(10^17 eV), discusses astrophysical and cosmogenic interpretations and notes that no unambiguous electromagnetic counterpart has been found.

entry.title: TAMBO project
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. A new contribution describes the Tau Air-Shower Mountain-Based Observatory, which aims to detect tau neutrinos from 1 PeV to 1,000 PeV. It would use up to 5,000 particle detectors on the face of a steep hill. This energy range lies between the reach of optical-Cherenkov and radio-based experiments and has largely suppressed backgrounds. The contribution also covers the TAMBITO prototype.

entry.title: PUEO balloon payload
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The PUEO collaboration presents the design and flight of a balloon-borne antenna array. It is intended to detect the Askaryan emission from interactions of ultrahigh-energy neutrinos. The motivation is that measuring the flux, flavour and energy of such neutrinos constrains how ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays are accelerated and propagate.

The second prototype adds a magnetic field compensation system and a liquid scintillator purification system.

entry.title: The paper examines the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars, which may contain Δ is
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper examines the neutrino emissivity of Δ-direct-Urca processes in neutron stars, which may contain Δ isobars alongside nucleons and hyperons. Its abstract says the contribution of this channel to neutrino emissivity had not been explicitly studied before. It matters to neutrino physicists because Urca processes are dominant neutron-star cooling mechanisms.

entry.title: The paper proves a no-go theorem for observing a Majorana phase through open two-flavour neutrino oscillations
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper proves a no-go theorem for observing a Majorana phase through open two-flavour neutrino oscillations. Every completely positive trace-preserving evolution covariant under rotations of the mass-coherence plane is exactly blind to the phase. A rate anisotropy in the environment can supply a phase reference, which defines what a decoherence-based Majorana-phase signal would require.

entry.title: The authors study how kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could constrain the primary cosmic-ray
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The authors study how kiloton-scale detectors such as Hyper-Kamiokande could constrain the primary cosmic-ray spectrum from the atmospheric neutrino flux. They find that future detectors can distinguish between cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, even allowing for cross-section and hadronic-interaction uncertainties. This turns atmospheric neutrinos into a probe of the cosmic-ray input rather than only a background.

entry.title: The paper builds a gauged U(1) L_μ−L_τ model with an ultralight vector boson that kinetically mixes with the p
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper builds a gauged U(1) L_μ−L_τ model with an ultralight vector boson that kinetically mixes with the photon and so adds a matter potential in the Sun, modifying MSW flavour conversion. It uses recent solar neutrino measurements from Borexino, SNO and Super-Kamiokande and discusses prospects for JUNO and XLZD. It shows solar neutrinos as a probe of light new vector bosons.

entry.title: The paper studies neutrino mass and thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, where masses a
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper studies neutrino mass and thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze model, where masses arise from a dimension-7 operator at tree level and a dimension-5 operator at one loop. The model gives sub-eV neutrino masses with new physics at the TeV scale. The authors examine whether thermal leptogenesis works, which they note differs from canonical seesaw leptogenesis.

entry.title: The paper asks whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be recorded as nuclear reco
entry.summary: AI-generated summary of the linked source; may contain errors. The paper asks whether neutrinos from past Galactic core-collapse supernovae could be recorded as nuclear recoil tracks in ancient minerals (paleodetectors). It includes different neutron-star masses, failed supernovae that form black holes, and the nuclear equation of state. It quantifies how the sensitivity increases for models with larger neutrino emission.
